[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cherry tomatoes need about 1-2 inches of water per week, either from rain or irrigation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Water should be applied at the base of the plant to prevent fungal diseases.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cherry tomatoes need good air circulation; plants should be spaced about 2-3 feet apart.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common tomato pests include hornworms, aphids, and whiteflies.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To control hornworms, hand-pick them or use Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To control aphids, spray with water or use neem oil.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To control whiteflies, use sticky traps or insecticidal soap.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Common diseases in cherry tomatoes include early blight, septoria leaf spot, and powdery mildew.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To prevent early blight, remove infected leaves, improve air circulation, and apply fungicide if necessary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To prevent septoria leaf spot, remove infected leaves and apply fungicide if necessary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] To prevent powdery mildew, remove infected leaves, improve air circulation, and apply fungicide if necessary.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Cherry tomatoes thrive in well-draining, fertile soil with a pH between 6.0 and 6.8.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Adding organic matter like compost or well-rotted manure can improve soil structure and fertility.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pruning cherry tomato plants promotes healthy growth and encourages fruiting.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Crop rotation helps avoid depleting soil nutrients and reduces disease risk.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Keeping the area around the plants clean helps prevent pests and diseases.  
[USER] The user appreciates the advice and plans to keep the tips in mind.  
[USER] The user is considering adding companion plants to their cherry tomato plants.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended companion plants include basil, marigold, chives, radish, and nasturtium for pest deterrence.
